resources.string: While you use other apps, Mudlet keeps your game connected and your scripts running, and shows a notification you can quit it from. Your scripts can also notify you, for example of a tell.

Android or a battery saver stopped Mudlet while you were using other apps, so your game was disconnected. To keep Mudlet running in the background, let it use the battery without restrictions: in Battery settings, choose Unrestricted, or on some phones Not optimised or No restrictions.
Mudlet stopped unexpectedly and was started again. You can tell the developers about it in Report a problem, where you see what a report holds before you send it. Nothing is sent unless you send it.

Show passwords as you type them
Passwords are typed into the input line, where they are shown and kept in the history. Turn this on for a game that hides everything you type, not only passwords.

A key with more than one key binding runs them all, not only the first. Off unless a game\'s scripts need it.

Text size, colours and the map
The app\'s screens take their colours from your wallpaper. Off, they use Mudlet\'s own. The game\'s text keeps the game\'s colours.
Buttons below the game\'s text for walking with one thumb: the eight compass directions, up, down, in and out. They make way for a keyboard, and need a screen tall enough for them.
Looking for a newer test build
Once a day, the app asks GitHub for the newest test build\'s number and tells you when there is a newer one. It sends nothing about you.
